public_rationale: A 2021 study comparing GPT-2 and GPT-3 found that untrained evaluators distinguished GPT-3 text from human writing at chance level, supporting improved naturalness [e1]. A separate 2021 comparison found reduced coverage of encyclopedic, commonsense and incoherence error annotations in GPT-3 relative to GPT-2 under matched sampling settings [e2]. These results support reductions in several kinds of mistakes within the claimed period [e2]. Off-prompt, math, and grammar and usage errors plateaued, so the gains were uneven [e2].
limitations: Humanlikeness is an indirect measure of fluency and does not establish factual correctness [e1].
The error comparison concerns generated English news, and results depend on sampling settings [e2].
These studies do not directly evaluate the January 30, 2023 ChatGPT update [e1, e2].
Reduced error coverage does not establish that developers individually patched particular mistakes or permanently eliminated them [e2].

our_interpretation: The comparison is between GPT-2 in 2019 and its GPT successors available by February 2, 2023.
The plain reading is smoother, more natural writing and a substantial reduction in errors, not elimination of all errors.
Addressed is read as reduced or corrected in later outputs; it does not require proof that developers individually patched particular examples.
Direct GPT-2/GPT-3 comparisons can establish improvements achieved within this interval without relying on later models.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations show more natural writing and meaningful reductions in multiple error categories in GPT successors relative to GPT-2.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations show no meaningful improvement in writing fluency or error incidence, or show systematic deterioration on those dimensions.

evidence.locator: Abstract; comparative results in Section 2.4 and Table 1
evidence.explanation: Under matched prompting, evaluators distinguished GPT-2 from human text more accurately than GPT-3 from human text across stories, news, and recipes. This supports improved naturalness, although humanlikeness is an indirect fluency measure.

evidence.excerpt: These error categories decrease with in-domain training (Grover) and larger model size (GPT-3).
evidence.explanation: Matched GPT-2/GPT-3 comparisons find reductions in encyclopedic, commonsense, and incoherence errors. Other categories plateau or behave less consistently, and generation settings affect the results.
